description: Direct endpoint attack: send an unsigned OIDC request object (alg=none) and check whether the authorization endpoint accepts and processes it.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must not accept an unsigned (alg=none) request object as an authentic proof of authorization request parameters; if accepted, attacker-controlled parameters could be consumed without integrity verification.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Authorization endpoint accepted an unsigned (alg=none) request object, indicating request-parameter proof integrity may be bypassed.
Control request-object probe did not return an HTTP status; cannot distinguish security enforcement from unsupported feature.

description: Brokered-flow attack: attempt token exchange with a subject_token that is not bound to the configured OIDC connector trust anchor (issuer/JWKS).
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex token exchange must verify the submitted subject_token against the configured connector trust anchor; a token minted under a different issuer/JWKS must not be consumed as if verified for this connector.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control token exchange failed; cannot attribute forged-token rejection/acceptance to proof-integrity enforcement vs setup issues.
Dex accepted a subject_token with a forged issuer/JWKS (trust-anchor substitution), indicating proof integrity failure in token exchange.

description: Direct endpoint attack: attempt semantic mismatch between outer query parameters and an unsigned request object to see if Dex consumes attacker-controlled semantics without verifying the proof.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: If Dex supports request objects, it must not allow an unsigned request object to override/alter the effective authorization request semantics (scope/redirect_uri/client_id) compared to what is verified/expected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control authorization request did not return an HTTP status; cannot interpret request-object behavior.
Dex accepted an unsigned request object probe; if processed, attacker can alter authorization request semantics without integrity.

description: Direct endpoint: attempt to override authorization request semantics using an unsigned request object (alg=none) and see if the endpoint accepts it (proof not verified but consumed).
invariant_hypothesis: I1: If an unsigned request object is accepted and processed, the authorization endpoint may consume attacker-controlled parameters without applying authenticity checks to the same semantic content.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Authorization endpoint accepted an unsigned (alg=none) request object, indicating proof semantics may be consumed without authenticity verification.
Unsigned request object was not rejected/unsupported (expected rejection or explicit unsupported behavior).

description: Brokered-flow: attempt token exchange using a subject_token that is a JWT with attacker-controlled kid (key id) pointing to an untrusted key; verify exchange is rejected (no key confusion). Includes a control password login to ensure client/session plumbing works.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must not accept a subject_token whose signature verifies only under an attacker-controlled key selection (kid injection) or untrusted JWKS; the consumed identity must match the verified proof under the configured connector trust anchor.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a token-exchange subject_token with attacker-controlled kid/untrusted signature, indicating proof semantics may be consumed without correct authenticity verification.
Control password login failed; token-exchange rejection could be due to setup/client issues rather than proof-integrity enforcement.

description: Brokered-flow: attempt token exchange using a JWT subject_token with alg=none (unsigned). Include a control token-exchange attempt using a plausible signed JWT format to distinguish 'always failing exchange' from 'signature enforcement'.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must reject unsigned JWTs (alg=none) presented as subject_token in token exchange; otherwise it may consume attacker-controlled claims without verifying authenticity under the connector trust policy.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted an unsigned (alg=none) JWT as subject_token in token exchange, indicating proof semantics may be consumed without authenticity verification.
Control token exchange failed; rejection of alg=none token may be due to connector/grant/client setup rather than signature enforcement.

description: Direct endpoint: attempt parameter smuggling via unsigned request object (alg=none) to override redirect_uri/scope semantics without signature verification
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must not consume authorization request semantics from an unsigned request object (alg=none); if it does, it violates proof integrity by using unverified semantics.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted an unsigned (alg=none) request object, indicating it may consume attacker-controlled authorization semantics without verifying authenticity (proof integrity failure).
Control password login failed; request-object results may be inconclusive due to client/grant misconfiguration rather than proof-integrity enforcement.

description: Brokered-flow: trust-anchor substitution attempt by presenting a JWT with attacker-controlled issuer/JWKS semantics; Dex must reject if connector issuer is fixed to the configured upstream
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must bind verification to the configured connector issuer/JWKS; it must not accept tokens that self-declare an attacker issuer and keys (trust-anchor substitution).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a subject_token that attempts to substitute the trust anchor via attacker-controlled issuer/JWKS semantics, indicating it consumed proof semantics not verified under the intended connector policy (proof integrity failure).
Control password login failed; token-exchange results may be inconclusive due to grant/client configuration rather than proof-integrity enforcement.

description: Direct endpoint: send an unsigned OIDC request object (alg=none) and check whether the authorization endpoint accepts it (proof consumed without verification). Include a baseline auth request without request object to distinguish 'endpoint down' from 'request object bypass'.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must not accept and process an unsigned (alg=none) request object; if it does, it may consume attacker-controlled authorization semantics without applying authenticity checks to the same semantic proof.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Authorization endpoint accepted an unsigned request object (alg=none), indicating request semantics may be consumed without authenticity verification (I1 proof integrity failure).
Baseline authorization request did not reach a normal auth response range; request-object test results may be inconclusive due to endpoint/config issues rather than proof-integrity enforcement.

description: Authorization-code replay: redeem the same authorization code twice and ensure the second redemption is rejected (one-time artifact). Includes identity verification after first redemption.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: An OAuth2/OIDC authorization code is a one-time artifact and must not be accepted more than once, even if replayed immediately.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Authorization code was accepted more than once (replay succeeded); auth codes must be one-time use.
Control failed: initial code exchange did not succeed, so replay result is not attributable to anti-replay enforcement.

description: Refresh-token rotation anti-replay: obtain refresh_token via password grant, exchange it for a new token (token-exchange), then attempt to reuse the old refresh_token again and expect rejection.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: If refresh token rotation is enabled, an old refresh token must not be accepted after it has been used to mint a new token (anti-replay).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control failed: password login did not succeed; refresh-token replay test is not attributable to anti-replay enforcement.
Control failed: first use of refresh token did not succeed; old-token reuse result is not meaningful.
Old refresh token was accepted after being used once; indicates missing refresh-token rotation or replay protection.

description: Revocation freshness: obtain a session token via password login, revoke it, then verify the token can no longer access /userinfo (should be rejected). Includes a second identity login to satisfy multi-identity requirement.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: After explicit revocation, the revoked session/access token must not be accepted for subsequent requests (anti-replay after revocation).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control failed: victim login did not succeed; revocation test is not meaningful.
Control failed: second identity login did not succeed; multi-identity baseline not established.
Revoked session token still accepted at /userinfo; indicates missing revocation enforcement (replay after revocation).
Revoked session token still accepted for protected resource access; indicates missing revocation enforcement.

description: Replay an old access token after a second login (re-auth) to check whether prior session artifacts remain valid beyond intended lifetime/rotation semantics.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: After a new login issues a new session_token, the previously issued session_token should not remain valid indefinitely; replaying the old token should be rejected (or at least not outlive its TTL).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Old session_token from first password login remained usable after a subsequent re-auth; indicates replay/overlong validity of a prior credential artifact.
Control logins failed; cannot attribute replay outcome to freshness enforcement.

description: I2: Reuse an old access/session token after a second successful password login (re-auth) to check whether prior session artifacts remain valid beyond intended lifetime/rotation semantics.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: After a user re-authenticates and obtains a new session token, the previously issued session token should not remain valid indefinitely; at minimum it must expire per TTL and should not be accepted if the deployment enforces single-session or short-lived tokens.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Old session token from first password login remained accepted after a second re-authentication; potential replay window beyond intended lifetime.
Control failed: second password login did not succeed, so old-token reuse result is not attributable to freshness enforcement.

description: I2: Token exchange control with a valid subject_token, then attempt exchange with a future-nbf subject_token (should be rejected). Includes second identity login for multi-identity requirement.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Dex token exchange must reject upstream tokens that are not yet valid (nbf in the future) while accepting a valid control token under the same connector/client context.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control failed: valid subject_token could not be exchanged; future-nbf rejection/acceptance cannot be attributed to freshness enforcement.
Dex accepted a subject_token with nbf far in the future during token exchange; not-yet-valid token was treated as fresh.

description: I2: Obtain refresh_token via password grant, then attempt to use the same refresh_token twice (refresh token replay). Includes second identity login for multi-identity requirement.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Refresh tokens are long-lived but must not be replayable beyond rotation policy; if rotation is enabled (default), reusing an already-used refresh_token should be rejected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control failed: refresh token could not be used once; replay result cannot be attributed to anti-replay enforcement.
Refresh token replay succeeded (old refresh_token accepted twice); anti-replay/rotation enforcement failed.

description: I2 anti-replay hardening: attempt to reuse the same password grant credentials to obtain multiple tokens; ensure Dex does not incorrectly treat password grant as one-time (should allow) but enforces token TTL by rejecting /userinfo after explicit revoke is unavailable here. This sequence instead checks that two logins yield distinct token accessors/identities and that both tokens remain valid independently (no unintended one-time artifact semantics).
invariant_hypothesis: I2: One-time artifacts must not be accepted more than once; password grant is NOT a one-time artifact, so Dex should issue fresh tokens on each login and not incorrectly bind/reject subsequent logins as replay. If Dex mistakenly treats the password exchange as one-time, the second login would fail (availability bug) rather than a security bug; however, if Dex reuses the same token/accessor across logins, it may indicate replayable artifacts or broken freshness semantics.

oracle_checks.assertion: user_alice_pwd_1_http_status == 200 AND user_alice_pwd_2_http_status == 200 AND user_alice_pwd_1_token_accessor != user_alice_pwd_2_token_accessor
oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex reused the same token accessor across two password-grant logins (freshness failure) or rejected the second login (unexpected one-time artifact semantics).
Re-authentication with the same credentials mapped to a different downstream identity, suggesting unstable session artifact binding that can enable replay/confusion.
Control identity failed to login or collided with Alice's identity, making freshness/replay conclusions unreliable.

description: OIDC state swap across two browser sessions: start two auth requests with different state values, then attempt to complete/exchange using the wrong session context (simulated by swapping state). Flow must remain session-bound and reject the spliced completion.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization responses must be bound to the initiating session via state; cross-session state swapping must not yield a valid token.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Token endpoint accepted an authorization code in a swapped/cross-session state context; flow is not coherently bound to the initiating session.
UserInfo succeeded after a state-swapped exchange attempt; indicates session splicing or unintended token issuance.

description: Authorization-code exchange without client authentication: attempt to redeem an auth code while omitting client_secret (and without relying on PKCE) to test whether the code is bound to the client.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization codes must be redeemable only by the correct client; missing client authentication must not succeed for a confidential client.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Authorization code was redeemed without client authentication (client_secret missing) for a confidential client; code is not coherently bound to the client.
UserInfo succeeded after unauthenticated code redemption attempt; indicates unintended token issuance or session confusion.

description: Authorization code replay: redeem the same auth code twice to test atomicity/order-preservation of the code flow (code must be one-time).
invariant_hypothesis: I3: An authorization code must be bound to a single successful redemption; a second redemption (even by the same client) must be rejected to prevent step reordering/replay within the FSM.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Authorization code was accepted more than once (second redemption succeeded), violating flow atomicity/order-preservation.

description: Code injection / cross-identity splicing: obtain a code in one browser session, then attempt to redeem it while authenticated as a different identity via password grant.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Steps from different sessions/principals must not be spliceable; a code minted for one user/session must not be redeemable to create a session for a different principal.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Attacker was able to redeem a code minted in a different session/principal context (code injection / session splicing).

description: Unsigned request object (alg=none) used to splice/override authorization parameters (client_id/redirect_uri/state) and potentially skip intended ordering/binding.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization request parameters must be coherently bound to the initiating session/client; an unsigned request object must not allow parameter splicing that changes flow binding (state/redirect/client) without rejection.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Unsigned request object (alg=none) was accepted, enabling potential parameter splicing that can break flow coherence.

description: PKCE skip attempt: start an auth request that includes a PKCE code_challenge, then attempt to redeem the resulting code without providing code_verifier (should be rejected to preserve flow coherence when PKCE was initiated). Includes a control redemption with the correct code_verifier.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: If the authorization request initiated PKCE (code_challenge), the token endpoint must require the matching code_verifier for that code; otherwise the multi-step flow can be spliced/short-circuited.

oracle_checks.assertion: user_victim_pkce_control_http_status == 200 AND user_victim_pkce_control_entity_id is not None
oracle_checks.violation_description: Control PKCE redemption failed; cannot attribute attack outcome to PKCE enforcement vs misconfiguration
Token endpoint accepted an authorization code initiated with PKCE without a valid code_verifier, enabling step-skipping/splicing of the code flow

description: Token exchange connector-binding test: perform a control token exchange using connector_id=mock, then attempt to exchange the same subject_token while specifying a different connector_id (should be rejected). This checks that the exchange is coherently bound to the intended upstream connector/session context.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Token exchange must be bound to the correct connector context; a subject_token validated under one connector must not be accepted under a different connector_id (prevents cross-connector splicing).

oracle_checks.assertion: user_alice_exchange_control_login_status == 200 AND user_alice_exchange_control_entity_id is not None
oracle_checks.violation_description: Control token exchange failed; cannot attribute wrong-connector outcome to connector binding vs setup/grant disablement
Token exchange accepted a subject_token under an unrelated connector_id, indicating cross-connector flow splicing / missing connector binding

description: I3 attack: start two concurrent OIDC auth code flows with different PKCE verifiers; attempt to redeem code from flow A using verifier from flow B (cross-session splicing). Includes a control redemption using the correct verifier for flow A.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization code redemption must be bound to the exact PKCE verifier (and thus the initiating browser session/flow). A code from flow A must not be redeemable with flow B's verifier.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control redemption for flow A failed; cannot attribute splice failure/success to PKCE/session binding enforcement.
Authorization code from flow A was redeemable using flow B's code_verifier (cross-session PKCE splicing), violating flow coherence.

description: I4 case_confusion: attempt to collapse two security-distinct principals by varying username case in password grant (e.g., 'Alice' vs 'alice').
invariant_hypothesis: I4: If the upstream principal identifier is case-sensitive, Dex must not normalize/case-fold it such that distinct principals map to the same downstream identity.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Case-variant usernames ('Alice' vs 'alice') collapsed into the same downstream identity (case-folding/normalization identity collision)

description: I4 cross_protocol_identity_merge: login via password as one principal, then obtain an OIDC code flow token for a different upstream principal that shares an email/username-like attribute; verify Dex does not merge them into one downstream identity.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: Distinct upstream principals authenticated via different mechanisms (password vs OIDC code flow) must not be merged into the same downstream identity solely due to shared attributes like email or display name.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Cross-protocol identity merge: password principal and OIDC principal collapsed into the same downstream identity

invariant_hypothesis: I4: Identities from different upstream principals/connectors must not be merged solely due to shared attributes like email/display name.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals

description: Attempt to escalate scopes/claims via RFC8693 token exchange after obtaining a limited-scope token via password grant; verify exchanged identity does not gain extra claims/policies beyond upstream intent.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: A token obtained with limited upstream intent (scope=openID email) must not be exchangeable into a token that carries additional claims (groups/profile/federated:id) or broader effective permissions without explicit upstream authorization and broker policy allowing it.

oracle_checks.assertion: user_escalated_exchange_login_status >= 400 OR (user_escalated_exchange_groups == user_limited_pwd_groups AND user_escalated_exchange_policies == user_limited_pwd_policies AND user_escalated_exchange_identity_policies == user_limited_pwd_identity_policies)
oracle_checks.violation_description: Token exchange expanded effective authorization (claims/policies) beyond the original limited-scope upstream intent.

description: Send an unsigned request object (alg=none) to the auth endpoint to see if attacker-controlled parameters (scope/client_id/redirect_uri) are accepted; then attempt to complete flow and verify no authorization escalation occurs.

description: Attempt to escalate scopes/claims during RFC8693 token exchange by using an ID token obtained with minimal scopes, then requesting expanded scopes in the exchange.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Exchanged token must not include claims/permissions beyond the upstream intent (originally granted scopes) and broker policy; expanded scopes in token exchange should be rejected or not reflected in resulting identity claims.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Token exchange accepted expanded scopes and returned group claims even though original upstream intent only requested 'openid email' (scope escalation via exchange).

description: Attempt to mint a token for a different audience via token exchange (audience=other client) using a valid subject token; verify the exchange is rejected (or at least does not yield a usable session). Includes a second identity as a control to ensure the system is responsive.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: A client must not be able to obtain tokens for an unauthorized audience/client via token exchange unless explicitly trusted by broker policy (trustedPeers).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Token exchange minted a token for an unauthorized audience/client without explicit trustedPeers/broker policy allowing cross-client issuance.
Control logins failed; token-exchange rejection cannot be attributed to authorization binding enforcement.

description: Probe whether Dex mints tokens for a different audience (client) via RFC8693 token exchange without explicit trustedPeers authorization (cross-client trust bypass). Uses two identities to ensure the system is responsive and to detect unintended permission/identity changes.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Token exchange must not allow a client to obtain tokens for an unauthorized audience (different client) unless broker policy explicitly allows it (e.g., trustedPeers). Effective permissions/claims must remain within UpstreamIntent ∩ BrokerPolicy.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted token exchange for an unauthorized audience (cross-client token minting) without explicit trustedPeers/broker policy authorization, violating authorization binding.
